steps.body:
From the one identity you know — **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1** (recall) — two more appear by division. Divide every term by **cos²θ**:

tan²θ + 1 = **sec²θ**.

Divide instead by **sin²θ**:

1 + cot²θ = **csc²θ**.

Three identities, one parent.

predict.prompt: The Pythagorean family all comes from one picture. If a formula in it carries a sign slip, what will the circle show?

options.label: The computed point mirrors off the true one the moment θ moves
Nothing — signs wash out when you square

predict.reveal: It mirrors off — a wrong sign is a wrong reflection, visible instantly. tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ is safe under squaring, but the family's unsquared members are not: pick each formula and watch which survives the drag.

widget.prompt: One point is plotted directly at 90° − θ; the candidates compute it from θ. Pick the family member without the sign slip and land θ on 60°.

ghostChoices.label: (sin θ, −cos θ)
ghostChoices.feedback: The sign slip: squaring would hide it — (−cos θ)² = cos²θ — which is why tan² + 1 = sec² can't catch it but the CIRCLE can. Watch the point mirror across the x-axis and detach as soon as θ leaves 0°.

widget.successFeedback: Glued at every θ. With tan θ = 3/4 the squared identity gives sec²θ = 9/16 + 1 = 25/16 — the entry above — and the picture you just held is why that always works: the family is one right triangle on the circle, and right signs keep it one triangle.
widget.lowFeedback: The formula holds — finish the drag to 60° and read the coincidence there.
widget.highFeedback: Past 60° — ease back; the reading is at 60°.

explanationVariants: sec θ = √(25/16) = 5/4 = 1.25 (positive for an acute θ).
√sec²θ = 5/4; the sign follows the quadrant, positive here.

widget.prompt: Continuing (acute θ), what is sec θ? (As a decimal.)

commonErrors.feedback: 1.5625 is sec²θ. Take the square root: √(25/16) = 5/4 = 1.25.
0.8 = cos θ. sec is its reciprocal, 1.25 — which matches √(sec²θ).

steps.body: These shine when **simplifying**: sec²θ − 1 collapses straight to **tan²θ**, and 1 − sin²θ becomes **cos²θ**. Spotting a Pythagorean pair inside a messy expression is the single most useful move in identity work.

explanationVariants: csc²θ − 1 = cot²θ, directly from 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ rearranged.
Move the 1: csc²θ − 1 is exactly cot²θ.

options.label: cot²θ
options.feedback: Right — rearrange 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ to get csc²θ − 1 = cot²θ.

options.label: tan²θ
options.feedback: tan²θ = sec²θ − 1 (the cosine-divided version). The sine-divided one gives csc²θ − 1 = cot²θ.
csc²θ − 1 isn't 1 unless csc²θ = 2. In general it's cot²θ.

explanationVariants: sin²θ + sin²θ·cot²θ = sin²θ(1 + cot²θ) = sin²θ · csc²θ = sin²θ/sin²θ = 1.
Factor sin²θ, apply the identity, then sin²θ · csc²θ = 1.

options.label: 1, after converting cot²θ to csc²θ and simplifying.
options.feedback: Right — factor sin²θ(1 + cot²θ) = sin²θ·csc²θ = sin²θ/sin²θ = 1.

options.label: sin²θ, after stopping before the cotangent term.
options.feedback: Factoring gives sin²θ(1 + cot²θ), and 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ = 1/sin²θ — the sin²θ cancels to 1.

options.label: cot²θ, after dropping the sine-squared factor.
options.feedback: Don't drop the first term: the FACTORED form sin²θ(1 + cot²θ) simplifies all the way to 1.

explanationVariants: (1 − cos²θ)·sec²θ = sin²θ·sec²θ = sin²θ/cos²θ = tan²θ. At θ = π/4, tan²θ = 1.
Recognize 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ first; the rest converts to tan²θ, which is 1 at π/4.
hints: Replace 1 − cos²θ using the parent identity.
1 − cos²θ = sin²θ, so the expression is sin²θ · sec²θ = sin²θ/cos²θ.

widget.prompt: Simplify (1 − cos²θ)·sec²θ to a single function, then evaluate at θ = π/4.

commonErrors.feedback: The simplified form is tan²θ; tan(π/4) = 1, so tan²(π/4) = 1, not 1/2.

takeaways: Divide sin²+cos²=1 by cos²θ → tan²+1 = sec²; by sin²θ → 1+cot² = csc².
Rearranged: sec²−1 = tan², csc²−1 = cot², 1−sin² = cos².
Spotting a Pythagorean pair is the master simplification move.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: combining two DIFFERENT angles — the sum and difference formulas.

concept.body: The family: sin²+cos²=1, tan²+1=sec², 1+cot²=csc². Rearrange any of them to collapse a '±1' expression into a single squared function.

explanationVariants: 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ, straight from the parent identity.
Move sin²θ across: what's left is cos²θ.

options.label: cos θ
options.feedback: Mind the square: 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ, not cos θ.

options.label: tan²θ
options.feedback: That comes from sec²θ − 1. Here 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ.
